Merge the Twitter probes: keep deal23-5 (the strongest trap) and replace ren-1 with a different rename event.

issues.problem: (1) All four outcomes fall in March to May 2023, before gpt-4o's cutoff, so they cannot separate the two models. (2) All four come from one correlated event cluster (the March 2023 banking crisis). (3) outcome_date is the failure date, not the date the trapped counterparty became known (bank-2: First Citizens deal 2023-03-26, not 03-10; bank-4: Flagstar 2023-03-19, not 03-12). (4) The horizons are 1 to 7 days, so a point-in-time model whose checkpoint is monthly or yearly would legitimately contain the outcome. (5) The headlines ('Full-Blown Crisis', 'Stay Calm') already signal distress.
issues.fix: Keep at most two (bank-1 for UBS, and bank-3 or bank-4). Set outcome_date to the counterparty announcement date. Add a flag requiring that the dated or PIT checkpoint cutoff is strictly before headline_date, not merely before outcome_date. Add one distressed-bank probe whose resolution came after Oct 2023, e.g. a 2023 NYCB headline (Liberty Strategic Capital rescue, 2024-03-06).

issues.problem: These repeat events already covered elsewhere: tech-1 and deal23-2 (Broadcom/VMware), tech-2 and deal22-1 (Adobe/Figma), tech-3 with ren-1 and deal23-5 (Musk/Twitter), late-3 and deal23-4 (Capital One/Discover), late-5 and ren-3 (Kellogg/Mars). The same world-knowledge fact is counted twice, which inflates confidence.
issues.fix: Keep one probe per event. Better still, turn each pair into a single paired design on purpose: a headline before the deal plus the announcement headline, scored jointly as one event. Replace the freed slots with new events.

issues.problem: Gold is 'none' for all 15, and the future counterparty is never named in the headline. A pure extraction model almost never invents a missing actor, so these probes will show about 0% leakage for every model and give false comfort. They also cannot be told apart from a model that always answers 'none'.
issues.fix: Rewrite about half as co-mention traps: headlines that name both future parties in a weaker relation, where gold is 'partners with'/'supplies'/'none' and a leaky model would upgrade it to 'acquires'. Examples: 'Spirit AeroSystems ... Boeing 737 fuselage supply' (gold supplies; Boeing agreed to buy Spirit in 2024); a pre-deal 'U.S. Steel Explores Strategic Alternatives' (Aug 2023; buyer Nippon Steel, Dec 2023); a 2023 'Exxon ... Pioneer' talks headline; 'Capital One, Discover' co-mentions before 2024-02. Add the other trap from the guideline: 'X agrees to be bought by an unnamed buyer' or 'X explores sale', where gold is NONE (counterparty not named) and the leak is filling in the real buyer.

issues.problem: The outcomes (2023-09-21, 2023-10-23, 2023-10-13) fall at or inside gpt-4o's cutoff month, so whether gpt-4o knows them is uncertain. They are labelled 'late' but do not separate the two models reliably.
issues.fix: Tag them known_to='edge' and report them separately, or replace them with outcomes from Jan to Sep 2024 (e.g. HPE/Juniper, Mars/Kellanova, Synopsys/Ansys 2024-01-16, Home Depot/SRS 2024-03-28).

issues.problem: outcome_date disagrees with future_status: late-4 has 2024-01-08 vs agreed 2024-01-09; late-5 has 2024-08-04 vs 2024-08-14; late-6 has 2024-03-01 vs 2024-07-01. Some probes date the rumour and others the agreement or completion.
issues.fix: Split the field into first_public_date (the first report) and resolution_date, and use one of them consistently for the cutoff test. late-5: 2024-08-04 first report, 2024-08-14 agreement. late-6: 2024-03-01 talks, 2024-07-01 agreement. late-4: 2024-01-08 report, 2024-01-09 agreement.

issues.problem: future_status is 'completed', which gives the same relation label (acquires) as PIT. A leaky model gives the same answer, so these probes cannot detect leakage in the relation task. deal23-3 (headline 2023-12-18) and deal23-4 (headline 2024-02-20) are also dated after gpt-4o's cutoff, so they are not past-reliability probes for gpt-4o at all. 'deal23' is a misleading prefix: deal23-1 is from 2022.
issues.fix: Recategorise them as controls, specifically future-agrees-with-PIT controls. Replace them with deals that failed after Oct 2023 and have headlines before 2023-10: e.g. Illumina/Grail unwind (2023-12 decision), Tapestry/Capri (announced 2023-08-10, blocked 2024-10-24, terminated 2024-11-14), Amex GBT/CWT (DOJ suit Jan 2024, abandoned Jun 2024). Rename the categories by outcome type, not by year.

issues.problem: The resolution (court block 2024-12-10, termination 2024-12-11) is at the edge of the 2026 model's guaranteed knowledge. The listed future_counterparty, C&S (divestiture buyer, Sept 2023), is the buyer of divested stores, not an acquirer of Albertsons, and a model is not wrong to know about it.
issues.fix: Tag it known_to='2026-edge'. Drop C&S from future_counterparties, or move it to a 'related_future_entities' field that is not scored as leakage.

issues.problem: 'FTX US Wins Auction for Its Assets' is an asset purchase. Under the guideline ('purchase of something that is not a company' is NONE), whether gold should be 'acquires' is debatable. Both models also know the outcome (Nov 2022).
issues.fix: Either state in the guideline that buying substantially all of a company's business or assets in bankruptcy counts as acquires, or replace the probe with an unambiguous 'to buy X' headline. Tag it known_to='both'.

issues.problem: 'Spirit Air' (Spirit Airlines) and 'Spirit AeroSystems' are different companies. That makes a useful confusion trap, but nothing marks it as one. future_counterparty 'Frontier' in deal22-3 is the earlier (Feb 2022) bidder, so it is past knowledge, not future.
issues.fix: Add a trap_type field (e.g. 'name_collision') to both. Remove Frontier from future_counterparties, or re-date it to Frontier's 2024-25 approaches.

issues.problem: The ticker 'X' (U.S. Steel) collides with X Corp's name (ren-1, deal23-5). This is useful but undocumented. The headline is after gpt-4o's cutoff, and the outcome (2025) is beyond the 2026 model's guaranteed knowledge.
issues.fix: Keep it as an explicit 'ticker_collision' trap. For the Nippon/US Steel event, add a pre-cutoff 'U.S. Steel Explores Options / Rejects Cleveland-Cliffs Bid' headline (Aug 2023), where gold is sells-none or acquires-rejected=none and the leak is naming Nippon Steel.

issues.problem: There are only 4 controls (11%). All 4 carry a positive relation, and none is a 'none' control, so there is no baseline false-positive rate for the 15 'none' future_counterparty probes. ctrl-3 ('Battery Supply Pact') could just as fairly be labelled 'partners with'. ctrl-4 should be re-checked against the source, since the verification is not documented.
issues.fix: Raise controls to about 25-30%. Match each trap category with controls of the same headline type and date that have no later event (e.g. earnings or layoff headlines for companies that were never acquired), so leakage = trap error rate minus control error rate. Accept 'partners with' as an alternative for ctrl-3, or add a guideline rule that a 'supply pact' is always supplies.

issues.problem: Several fields are inconsistent. Ticker format mixes 'VMW US' and 'VMW', 'TWTR US' and 'TWTR'. future_ticker sometimes means the subject's new ticker, sometimes a spin-off's ticker (ren-3, ren-4), and sometimes an IPO ticker (tech-2). There is no field saying which model is expected to know the outcome. 'deal_status_pit' is not in the guideline.
issues.fix: Standardise tickers to Bloomberg 'TICKER EXCH'. Define future_ticker as the subject entity's own ticker after the change. Add known_to: {gpt4o: bool, model2026: bool} computed from resolution_date against cutoffs 2023-10-31 and 2024-12-31 (edge = ±1 month). Add trap_type. Either score deal_status or drop it.

missing: Entity-level rename traps where the headline uses the old name, so a leaky model normalises it to the new one. Before gpt-4o's cutoff: Facebook to Meta, Square to Block, Royal Dutch Shell to Shell, Raytheon Technologies to RTX, Total to TotalEnergies. After it (only the 2026 model knows): NYCB to Flagstar Financial, the 3M health unit to Solventum, General Electric to GE Aerospace.
Unnamed-counterparty traps: 'X explores sale', 'X agrees to be acquired' or 'X draws takeover interest' with no buyer named, where gold is NONE and the leak is filling in the real future buyer.

Co-mention upgrade traps: both future deal parties are named in a supply, partnership or lawsuit relation, and a leaky model upgrades it to 'acquires' (e.g. Spirit AeroSystems supplying Boeing, or a pre-2024 Capital One / Discover co-mention).
Role-reversal or direction traps: the earlier headline has A investing in or selling to B, and later B acquires A. This tests whether subject and object flip.
Rumoured deals that never happened: gold 'acquires' (rumoured), the future says nothing happened, and a leaky model drops or negates it. None of the current probes has a rumour-to-nothing outcome.

Leak-induced dropping of entities: companies that later went bankrupt or vanished (FTX, SVB, Credit Suisse, WeWork), where a leaky model might write the successor name instead of the name in the headline.

Traps on other predicates: there are none for 'partners with', 'sells', 'invests in' or 'sues'. Examples: a Microsoft/OpenAI investment later restructured, a stake that was later sold off, a partnership that later became a takeover.
Name-collision and ticker-collision traps, explicitly tagged: Spirit vs Spirit, X (U.S. Steel) vs X Corp, Block Inc vs H&R Block, Meta vs Meta Materials.

PERSON leakage traps: surname-only headlines where the person later changed role (Boeing CEO Calhoun, Twitter CEO Agrawal, SVB CEO Becker), checking that the model does not add or replace people using later knowledge.
Negative controls with gold 'none' and no later event, matched by headline type and date to the future_counterparty probes, so hallucination can be told apart from leakage.

Probes placed so the dated or PIT checkpoint matters: pairs with the same event and headlines just before vs just after the checkpoint cutoff, to test whether the dated model is leak-free at its own granularity.
A known_to / cutoff-window field and a trap_type field, so results can be stratified by which model should know the outcome.
critic.balance:
By category: 5 rename_ticker, 15 future_counterparty, 11 outcome_status and 4 control (35 probes). future_counterparty takes 43% of the set, and all 15 of its golds are 'none'. Gold relations: 17 none, 12 acquires, 2 invests in, 2 supplies, 1 sells, 1 sues, 0 partners with. The set is mostly acquires-or-none, so a model that says 'none' whenever no deal is named scores well on everything except the deal headlines.

By who knows the outcome (gpt-4o cutoff about Oct 2023; 2026 model at least to late 2024):
- Known to both: ren-1, ren-2, ren-3, bank-1..4, tech-1..5, deal22-5, deal22-6, deal23-5. That is about 16 probes. None of them can separate the two models, and 4 of them are one correlated banking-crisis week.
- Edge of gpt-4o's cutoff: late-1, late-2, deal23-1.
- Known only to the 2026 model: ren-4, late-3, late-4, late-5, late-6, deal22-1, deal22-3, deal22-4, deal23-2, with deal22-2 at its edge. That is about 9 to 10.
- Beyond both (or not guaranteed): ren-5, deal23-3 (resolved 2025), deal23-4 (completion 2025).
- 7 headlines are themselves dated after gpt-4o's cutoff (ren-4, ren-5, late-3, late-5, late-6, deal23-3, deal23-4). For gpt-4o these test out-of-distribution handling, not leakage.

Of the 11 outcome_status probes, only 7 have a future that changes the relation label: the 6 deal22 probes flip acquires to none, and deal23-5 flips none to acquires. The 4 'completed' deal23 probes do not change the label. After de-duplication (Twitter x3, Figma x2, VMware x2, Discover x2, Kellogg x2), about 29 distinct events remain.

Target: about 40 probes. Roughly 30% known only to the 2026 model, 30% known to both, and 25-30% matched controls including 'none' controls. At least 3 probes each for renames that change the headline name, unnamed-counterparty traps, co-mention upgrade traps and label-flipping outcome traps. Keep one probe per event, and make every outcome horizon longer than the dated model's checkpoint interval.
